title: Ethiopian Wedding Feast
community: All of Ethiopia — the traditional wedding feast
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Wedding Feast — the complete traditional Ethiopian wedding meal for 50 guests: Doro Wat (ETH061), Key Wat (ETH021), Tibs (ETH022), Kitfo (ETH029), Ayib (ETH096), Gomen (ETH106), Beyaynetu (ETH121), Tej (ETH215), and Difo Dabo (ETH004). The grandest meal in Ethiopian food culture.
longDesc: The Ethiopian wedding feast is the maximum expression of Ethiopian hospitality — a multi-day celebration of cooking that feeds an entire community. The scale requires community effort: neighbours cook together for days.
steps: 2 days before: cook Key Wat (huge pot). Prepare Doro Wat stock.
1 day before: complete Doro Wat. Prepare all fasting dishes.
Wedding day morning: fresh Tibs, Kitfo, fresh Ayib.
Wedding day: assemble the grand mesob. Coffee ceremony throughout.
chefTips: Ethiopian wedding cooking is community cooking — it cannot be done alone.
Scale every recipe: wedding quantities require large clay or metal pots.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian wedding cooking uses entirely local ingredients — the most sustainable feast format.
servedWith: At the Ethiopian wedding table — guests eat communally in groups
healthBenefits: Ethiopian wedding feast provides complete nutrition from every food group.
culturalNote: The Ethiopian wedding feast is the highest expression of hospitality — 'ye-serg mgib' (wedding food) is the standard by which all other Ethiopian food is measured. When an Ethiopian says something is 'as good as wedding food', they mean it cannot be better.
